title: You Wanted a Fence. You Got a Stadium.
description:
You only wanted a garden fence.

The first part is how a fence really goes in: a post hole about 600 mm deep, a little gravel so water drains away, fast-setting concrete round the post, a gravel board to keep the timber off the wet ground, then a 1.83 m panel. In England a fence can usually be up to 2 m high without planning permission, as long as it is not next to a road (listed buildings and some conservation areas differ).

Everything after the football comes over is a joke. Please do not build a dome.

Fence sources:
- Jacksons Fencing, How deep to dig fence posts: https://www.jacksons-fencing.co.uk/the-edit/how-deep-to-dig-fence-posts
- Wickes, How to install a fence: https://www.wickes.co.uk/how-to-guides/garden-landscaping/install-a-fence
- Planning Portal, Fences, gates and garden walls: https://www.planningportal.co.uk/permission/common-projects/fences-gates-and-garden-walls/planning-permission
- Homebuilding & Renovating, How to build a fence: https://www.homebuilding.co.uk/advice/how-to-build-a-fence

How many of next door's footballs are in your garden? Tell me below - and subscribe for more.
